Meeting header
Date: 2025-12-10
Time: 14:00 ET

Recorded: Yes

[00:00] Amy Chen (AE - Redwood): ok everyone thanks for joining, uh i'll kick us off. Amy from Redwood here, with jon our se and priya on cs. quick roll call?
[00:14] Dr. Neha Patel (Dir. ML Ops - Atlanta Health): Neha here, sarah and mark too. morning.
[00:20] Sarah Lowe (CTO - Atlanta Health): morning all, hope you got our incident notes.
[00:28] Jon Reyes (SE - Redwood): yep saw them, thanks for sending, we read through the timeline.
[00:35] Amy Chen: great, agenda - usage/cost trends, reliability review, dedicated pilot discussion, security questions, and wrap with next steps. we'll try to keep to 40 mins.
[01:05] Mark Reynolds (PM - Atlanta Health): sounds good. quick context, last quarter we onboarded 3 new endpoints and usage spiked about 38% month over month, so cost line items are a bit higher.
[01:30] Amy Chen: got it, and that's visible in the dashboard - priya, can you pull the usage?
[01:36] Priya Nair (CSM - Redwood): yeah pulling now, the per-route breakdown shows embeddings up 42%, chat generations 33%, average token length increased slightly.
[02:05] Dr. Patel: embedding costs are the big pain, we're feeding nightly batches for search re-indexing. curious if caching or quantization recommendations would make sense.
[02:20] Jon Reyes: absolutely, for embeddings batching by 4-8 gives huge wins, and if you can switch to a quantized emb model we can save ~30% compute. but need to balance accuracy.
[02:45] Luis Gomez (Infra): quick Q - are those quantized models supported on our on-prem GPUs? we run Ampere A10s.
[02:58] Jon Reyes: A10s are fine for int8/4 quant. there are some kernel choices, we can validate. i'll add that to the perf test.
[03:22] Sarah: can you share the expected delta in latency if we enable batching? our search needs sub-150ms 99th pct for interactive UX.
[03:35] Jon: batching can add a few ms on median but it usually helps throughput; we can do dynamic batching with tight latency SLOs to keep 99th under 150ms, depends on qps distribution.
[04:00] Amy: ok onto reliability - Neha you mentioned two incidents last month? can you summarize?
[04:12] Dr. Patel: yeah, 11/18 had a region outage, a fallback to tier-2 model happened but some sessions timed out; we saw an error spike for about 22 minutes. logs attached in the incident doc.
[04:35] Jon: right, looks like the smart routing fallback worked but we had a config that waited too long before switching to the cheaper model variant, that delay caused client retries and amplifed latencies.
[04:50] Amy: note to self: review fallback thresholds.
[05:02] Dr. Patel: also curious about KV cache persistence across restarts, we lost cold cache and that increased token counts during recovery window.
[05:18] Jon: KV cache warms in minutes but if the workload has many unique prefixes it will still be heavier. for private deployments we can snapshot KV to speed warmup.
[05:45] Tara Singh (Security - Atlanta Health): security question: we need to see updated SOC2 reports, kms integration details, and audit log export formats.
[05:58] Amy: yes, we have SOC2 Type II and KMS integration with both AWS KMS and customer-managed HSM. i'll share the security pack after this call.
[06:12] Priya: adding that as an action item.
[06:20] Mark: timeline wise we're looking at a pilot for dedicated capacity starting early january, ideally a 6-week pilot to validate perf/cost. is that feasible?
[06:35] Amy: feasible, jon can scope the dedicated pool size and run acceptance tests. the pilot would need an order form though.
[06:50] Jon: for sizing, tell us target rps and 99th latency target and we'll propose GPU counts, batch configs, and estimated monthly cost.
[07:10] Mark: baseline - 120 rps peak with p99 under 150ms and 95% of traffic at <80ms.
[07:25] Jon: ok noted.
[07:38] Dr. Patel: cost...our CFO wants a clear delta hosted vs dedicated. our current avg token cost is a bit high because of small bursts. any ballpark?
[07:52] Amy: early estimate - dedicated typically saves 25-40% at your scale, but depends on model choice and quantization. we'll send a detailed per-route cost model.
[08:08] Sarah: do you support per-route SLA? some of our endpoints are critical and others are batch-only.
[08:18] Priya: yes we can configure SLA tiers and routing policies to keep critical routes on reserved capacity while less critical go to hosted.
[08:30] Luis: what's the onboarding for private VPC? network whitelisting, cross-account roles?
[08:42] Jon: we do VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink, cross-account IAM roles for control plane, and customers can deploy the private runtime in their VPC for a fully isolated setup.
[09:00] Tara: encryption at rest - if we bring our own KMS, can we rotate keys? audit logs need to show key usage per-tenant.
[09:12] Amy: yes BYOK supported, rotation is customer-managed, we can expose key usage logs in the audit export. will share sample export.
[09:30] Dr. Patel: on the model side, are you recommending any specific open models for clinical notes? we care about hallucination risk.
[09:42] Jon: we recommend smaller curated models with medical finetune where possible, and run RLHF/evals against your prompt sets. Redwood Optimize can run regression alerts.
[10:05] Mark: can Redwood run evals on our PII redaction prompts? we'd like automated checks.
[10:15] Priya: yes, we can ingest your eval prompt set and set up continuous checks; we'll need a sanitized sample.
[10:25] Dr. Patel: note, some of our data is residency constrained to GA, any issues with region?
[10:36] Amy: we support regional routing; for Private deployments you can keep data in your VPC region. hosted we have region options in NA and EU.
[10:50] Luis: when you say "support" region, is data at rest guaranteed to not leave region? that's a requirement for some contracts.
[11:02] Amy: for hosted we provide regionally-restricted clusters and contractual data residency options; for strict residency you should consider Private.
[11:20] Mark: ok good.
[11:36] Jon: back to perf - i'll propose a test plan: 1) cold start warmup test 2) sustained peak at 120 rps for 30m 3) failover simulation to verify fallback policy. we'll share test script.
[12:00] Dr. Patel: would like to include warmup snapshot test for KV cache.
[12:10] Jon: noted.
[12:24] Sarah: in terms of observability, we need token-level cost dashboards and trace correlation to our distributed traces. is there an integration?
[12:36] Priya: we have trace hooks and can ingest trace IDs; token-level cost is available in the console and via an API export.
[12:50] Tara: on compliance - can you provide a sample DPA and data flows for legal? our legal team asked.
[13:02] Amy: yes, i'll include DPA and data flow diagrams in the security pack.
[13:18] Mark: onboarding blockers? we already tested some endpoints in staging. any surprises?
[13:28] Jon: only thing is the fallback thresholds and KV snapshotting mentioned. those are config items not blockers.
[13:40] Dr. Patel: curious about contract terms - if pilot shows >40% savings do we get a look at reserved pricing?
[13:52] Amy: pilot outcomes can be used to negotiate reserved capacity commits; we'll involve sales ops if you hit that threshold.
[14:08] Sarah: any maintenance windows? we're sensitive to restarts during business hours.
[14:20] Jon: we have rolling upgrades with maintenance windows usually scheduled off-hours, can coordinate.
[14:36] Amy: quick pause - any other pressing items?
[14:48] Mark: one ask - can Redwood share the benchmark spreadsheet you used for similar healthcare customers?
[14:58] Jon: yes, i'll attach the benchmark sheet and a sample config.
[15:15] Dr. Patel: thank you.
[15:25] Amy: ok moving to proposed timeline and next steps: we're proposing pilot start 2026-01-05, 6 weeks, acceptance tests by week 4, final review end of pilot.
[15:40] Mark: that aligns with our product timeline.
[15:52] Amy: recap of action items - amy to send security pack, jon to run perf test and share bench, priya to draft pilot success criteria. any additions?
[16:10] Tara: please include SOC2 auditor contact info in the pack.
[16:24] Amy: will do.
[16:35] Dr. Patel: on the cost model, please include per-route examples with our actual usage numbers.
[16:45] Amy: noted, we'll use today's dashboard numbers.
[17:00] Jon: small note - during the fallback incident we saw increased client retries; recommend exponential backoff on client side to avoid retry storms.
[17:18] Mark: will add.
[17:30] Sarah: anything on support SLAs for pilot?
[17:38] Priya: pilot includes dedicated CSM support and 24/7 SE on-call for the ramp period.
[17:50] Amy: perfect.
[18:02] Dr. Patel: okay that's helpful. thanks everyone.
[18:15] Amy: we'll follow up with the deck and security docs by Friday 12/12. jon will start perf runs tomorrow. priya will draft pilot criteria.
[18:30] Mark: closing note - please cc our procurement contact when sharing order details.
[18:40] Amy: will do. thanks all, we'll send notes and record action items.
[18:50] Amy: end call.
